title: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk | The Father of Modern Turkey
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 哈喽，哈喽哈喽，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听迷人的故事，了解世界上奇怪而美妙的事物，同时还能提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today is the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on the very loose theme of the fall of the Ottoman Empire and the birth of modern Turkey.
sentences.zh: 我是阿拉斯泰尔·巴奇（Alastair Budge），今天是另一个三集迷你系列的开篇，这次的主题大致围绕着奥斯曼帝国的衰落和现代土耳其的诞生。

sentences.en: In part one, today’s episode, we are going to talk about probably the most requested subject in the history of this show: the life of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the father of modern Turkey.
sentences.zh: 在第一部分，也就是今天的节目中，我们将讨论本节目历史上呼声最高的主题：现代土耳其之父——穆斯塔法·凯末尔·阿塔图尔克（Mustafa Kemal Atatürk）的一生。

sentences.en: In part two, we are going to talk about the life of a very different and less well-known figure, Ali Pasha – The so-called “Lion of Ioannina”.
sentences.zh: 在第二部分中，我们将讨论一个非常不同且不那么知名的人物——阿里·帕夏（Ali Pasha），也就是被称为“约阿尼纳之狮”的人。

sentences.en: And in part three, we will turn to Cyprus, the Mediterranean island split in two, and home to one of Europe’s last great unresolved conflicts.
sentences.zh: 第三部分，我们将转向地中海被一分为二的岛屿塞浦路斯，这里是欧洲最后一个未解决的重大冲突的发源地之一。

sentences.en: Right then, let’s get right into it, and talk about the father of modern Turkey.
sentences.zh: 好勒，让我们直接切入正题，聊聊现代土耳其之父。

sentences.en: On the 15th of October, 1927, the then President of Turkey stood up to give a speech.
sentences.zh: 1927年10月15日，时任土耳其总统起立发表了一场演讲。

sentences.en: To say it was “not short” would be something of an understatement.
sentences.zh: 如果要说它“不短”，那可真是有些低调了。

sentences.en: It took him 36 hours to finish, and was broken up over six days.
sentences.zh: 他花了36个小时才讲完，演讲分成了六天进行。

sentences.en: It was called Nutuk, or “The Speech”, in English, and it has become one of the most important historical documents in Turkish history.
sentences.zh: 它被称为 Nutuk，在英语中意为“演讲”，它已成为土耳其历史上最重要的历史文献之一。

sentences.en: Now, you might think, “well, Turkey, or at least the geographical area of Turkey, does have a long and storied history.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会想，“嗯，土耳其，或者说土耳其的地理区域，确实有着悠久而传奇的历史。

sentences.en: The Persians, the founding of Constantinople, the eastern Roman Empire, then the Byzantine Empire, the Ottoman Empire, and so on.
sentences.zh: 波斯人、君士坦丁堡的建立、东罗马帝国，然后是拜占庭帝国、奥斯曼帝国，等等。

sentences.en: There’s a lot to get through, so no wonder it took him so long!”
sentences.zh: 有太多内容要讲了，难怪他花了这么长时间！”

sentences.en: In fact, he didn’t talk about any of this, at least, not in any real detail.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他没有谈论任何这些，至少没有详细谈论。

sentences.en: The history of Turkey, as per this speech, started on the 19th of May, 1919.
sentences.zh: 根据这场演讲，土耳其的历史始于1919年5月19日。

sentences.en: This is the date when the speaker, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, landed at the town of Samsun, a port town on the southern side of The Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 这一天，演讲者穆斯塔法·凯末尔·阿塔图尔克在黑海南部的一个港口小镇萨姆松（Samsun）登陆。

sentences.en: The speech went on, and in it Atatürk presented the situation Turkey found itself in at that time.
sentences.zh: 演讲继续进行，阿塔图尔克在演讲中阐述了当时土耳其所处的境地。

sentences.en: Or rather, the situation in which the country we now know as Turkey found itself.
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，是我们现在所知的土耳其这个国家当时所处的境地。

sentences.en: The modern Republic of Turkey was, at that time, part of the Ottoman Empire—the vast, multi-ethnic empire that had ruled large parts of the Middle East, North Africa, and southeastern Europe for over six centuries.
sentences.zh: 当时的现代土耳其共和国是奥斯曼帝国的一部分——这个庞大的多民族帝国曾统治中东、北非和东南欧的大部分地区长达六个多世纪。

sentences.en: At its peak, in the late 17th century, it ruled over 5.2 million kilometres squared, covering much of modern Greece and the Balkan area, Syria, Iraq, Israel, Lebanon, and North Africa.
sentences.zh: 在其鼎盛时期的17世纪末，它统治着520万平方公里的土地，涵盖了现代希腊和巴尔干地区的大部分、叙利亚、伊拉克、以色列、黎巴嫩和北非。

sentences.en: It was a gigantic territory, greater even than the Roman Empire at its height.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的领土，甚至比全盛时期的罗马帝国还要大。

sentences.en: For hundreds of years, it had been one of the most powerful empires in the world, feared by European kings and emperors alike.
sentences.zh: 数百年来，它一直是世界上最强大的帝国之一，令欧洲国王和皇帝闻风丧胆。

sentences.en: Its armies had marched as far as Vienna, its navy controlled the Mediterranean, and its capital, Constantinople, was a city of immense wealth and influence.
sentences.zh: 它的军队曾一路进军维也纳，它的海军控制着地中海，其首都君士坦丁堡是一座拥有巨大财富和影响力的城市。

sentences.en: But it had past its peak, and by the late 19th century, the empire was in deep decline.
sentences.zh: 但它已经过了鼎盛时期，到19世纪末，帝国已经急剧衰落。

sentences.en: European diplomats and commentators had been watching its decline for decades, and had taken to calling it “the sick man of Europe”.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，欧洲的外交官和评论员一直在密切关注它的衰落，并开始称它为“欧洲病夫”。

sentences.en: Now, we’ll get into how it eventually collapsed in a minute, but first it's worth briefly touching on some of the reasons for the decline of the Ottoman Empire, because they help explain the rise of Atatürk.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们一会儿再探讨它是如何最终崩溃的，但首先值得简要谈谈奥斯曼帝国衰落的一些原因，因为这有助于解释阿塔图尔克的崛起。

sentences.en: Firstly, as is often the case with great empires, corruption and mismanagement had weakened the empire from within.
sentences.zh: 首先，正如伟大帝国常有的那样，腐败和管理不善从内部削弱了帝国。

sentences.en: Secondly, a series of military defeats had stripped it of territory.
sentences.zh: 其次，一系列军事失败剥夺了它的领土。

sentences.en: And thirdly, it was just too large and had too many competing different ethnic and religious groups—the Arabs, the Greeks, the Armenians, and the Slavs, to name but a few.
sentences.zh: 第三，它实在太大了，有着太多相互竞争的不同民族和宗教群体——仅举几例，就有阿拉伯人、希腊人、亚美尼亚人和斯拉夫人都。

sentences.en: This was an era of nationalist movements, and, perfectly reasonably you might argue, these groups wanted a country to call their own, they didn’t want to just be subsumed, swallowed up, by an empire to which they didn’t feel a strong sense of allegiance.
sentences.zh: 这是一个民族主义运动的时代，而且你完全可以合情合理地认为，这些群体想要一个属于他们自己的国家，他们不想被一个他们没有强烈效忠感的帝国所吞并。

sentences.en: Then came the First World War. It was bad news for everyone, but particularly bad news for the Ottoman Empire, which by this time was no longer ruled by a strong sultan but by a group of military leaders known as the ‘Three Pashas.’
sentences.zh: 接着第一次世界大战爆发了。这对所有人来说都是坏消息，但对奥斯曼帝国而言尤其如此，此时统治它的已不再是强有力的苏丹，而是一群被称为“三帕夏”的军事领导人。

sentences.en: These men led the empire into World War I, making the fateful decision to side with Germany and Austria-Hungary.
sentences.zh: 这些人将帝国带入了第一次世界大战，做出了与德国和奥匈帝国结盟的命运攸关的决定。

sentences.en: It was a disastrous decision, the nail in the coffin for the sick man of Europe.
sentences.zh: 这是一个灾难性的决定，是压垮欧洲病夫的最后一根稻草。

sentences.en: The Ottomans lost battles on multiple fronts, from the deserts of Arabia to the mountains of the Caucasus.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼人在多个战线上失利，从阿拉伯的沙漠到高加索的山脉。

sentences.en: Hundreds of thousands of soldiers were killed, an estimated 1.5% of the population.
sentences.zh: 数十万士兵丧生，估计占总人口的1.5%。

sentences.en: By the time the war ended in 1918, the Ottoman Empire was effectively finished.
sentences.zh: 到1918年战争结束时，奥斯曼帝国实际上已经完蛋了。

sentences.en: And if that wasn’t bad enough, its enemies—the victorious Allied powers of Britain, France, and Italy—were now circling like vultures.
sentences.zh: 如果这还不够糟糕的话，它的敌人——胜利的盟军英国、法国和意大利——现在正像秃鹰一样盘旋。

sentences.en: They had won the war, and they planned to carve up the Ottoman Empire among themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们赢得了战争，并计划在彼此之间瓜分奥斯曼帝国。

sentences.en: And they did, or at least, they tried to.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这么做了，或者说，他们尝试了。

sentences.en: Under the terms of the Treaty of Sèvres, which was signed in 1920, huge parts of the Ottoman Empire were handed over to foreign powers.
sentences.zh: 根据1920年签署的《色佛尔条约》（Treaty of Sèvres）的条款，奥斯曼帝国的庞大地区被移交给了外国列强。

sentences.en: Greece occupied the western region of Anatolia, of modern-day Turkey, while Italy took the south.
sentences.zh: 希腊占领了现代土耳其的安纳托利亚西部地区，而意大利则占领了南部。

sentences.en: The British controlled Mesopotamia and Palestine.
sentences.zh: 英国控制了美索不达米亚和巴勒斯坦。

sentences.en: The French took Syria and Lebanon. Even the Ottoman capital, Constantinople, or Istanbul as it's now called, was occupied by Allied troops.
sentences.zh: 法国夺取了叙利亚和黎巴嫩。甚至奥斯曼帝国的首都君士坦丁堡（现名伊斯坦布尔）也被盟军占领。

sentences.en: The Ottoman Empire was already seriously down from its peak, having gone from over 5 million kilometres squared to 1.6 million on the eve of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼帝国已经从其巅峰时期严重下滑，在一战前夕，领土从500多万平方公里缩减到160万平方公里。

sentences.en: And after the Treaty of Sèvres, it was left with a chunk of land in the middle of Anatolia, less than 500,000 kilometres squared, around the size of Sweden.
sentences.zh: 而在《色佛尔条约》签订后，它只剩下安纳托利亚中部的一块土地，面积不到50万平方公里，大约和瑞典差不多大。

sentences.en: To many, it seemed as though Turkey would soon be reduced to nothing more than a rump state —a tiny, powerless remnant of the once-great empire.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，土耳其似乎很快就会沦为一个残余国家——一个曾经伟大帝国的微小而无力的残余。

sentences.en: So, enter stage right, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.
sentences.zh: 于是，舞台右侧出场，穆斯塔法·凯末尔·阿塔图尔克。

sentences.en: Before we get into exactly what he did, let me tell you a little about his early life, as this also helps you get a taste for quite how multi-ethnic the region was, how over the years its various towns and cities have switched allegiances, and even names.
sentences.zh: 在我们深入探讨他具体做了什么之前，让我先向你介绍一下他的早年生活，因为这也有助于你体会该地区是多么地具有多民族性，多年来其各个城镇是如何改变阵营甚至名字的。

sentences.en: Atatürk was born in 1881 in the city of Salonica, which at the time was part of the Ottoman Empire, but today is in Greece, and it has a different name: Thessaloniki.
sentences.zh: 阿塔图尔克于1881年出生在萨洛尼卡（Salonica）市，当时该市是奥斯曼帝国的一部分，但今天它属于希腊，并且有一个不同的名字：塞萨洛尼基（Thessaloniki）。

sentences.en: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was not his real name, at least at birth.
sentences.zh: 穆斯塔法·凯末尔·阿塔图尔克并不是他的真名，至少在出生时不是。

sentences.en: Both Kemal and Atatürk came after, for reasons we’ll get to in a minute.
sentences.zh: “凯末尔”和“阿塔图尔克”都是后来才有的，原因我们一会儿会讲到。

sentences.en: The only name he came into the world with was Mustafa.
sentences.zh: 他来到这个世界时唯一的全名就是穆斯塔法。

sentences.en: If this sounds unusual, it wasn’t. It was fairly customary in the Ottoman Empire for children not to be given a surname, as they would typically acquire other names, other ways of identifying themselves, later on in life.
sentences.zh: 如果这听起来很不寻常，其实并非如此。在奥斯曼帝国，不给儿童起姓氏是相当普遍的习俗，因为他们通常会在日后的生活中通过其他名字或方式来表明自己的身份。

sentences.en: In terms of his parents, he came from a modest background; his father was a customs officer, and his mother was a devout Muslim.
sentences.zh: 至于他的父母，他出身于一个普通家庭；他的父亲是一名海关官员，母亲是一位虔诚的穆斯林。

sentences.en: His mother reportedly pushed for the young boy to have a religious education, to be schooled in a madras, but he went down a different path.
sentences.zh: 据报道，他的母亲曾力劝这个小男孩接受宗教教育，在一所伊斯兰学校（madrasa）上学，但他却走上了不同的道路。

sentences.en: After his father died, when the boy was only 7 years old, he convinced his mother to let him enrol in a military school.
sentences.zh: 在他7岁那年父亲去世后，他劝说母亲让自己进入一所军事学校。

sentences.en: And it was there that he got the name “Kemal”, which means “perfection” or “maturity” in Turkish.
sentences.zh: 正是在那里，他得到了“凯末尔”这个名字，在土耳其语中意为“完美”或“成熟”。

sentences.en: His maths teacher, so the legend goes, was so impressed by his intelligence and discipline that he gave him this nickname.
sentences.zh: 据传说，他的数学老师对他的聪明才智和纪律性印象深刻，于是给了他这个绰号。

sentences.en: And it was there, in military school, that he became fascinated with the idea of change.
sentences.zh: 也正是在那里，在军事学校里，他开始对变革的理念着迷。

sentences.en: This was at a time when it was patently clear to anyone, from the Sultan to the teenage boy at military school, that the Ottoman Empire was already in deep decline.
sentences.zh: 当时，从苏丹到军事学校的少年，任何人都显而易见地看出奥斯曼帝国已经在急剧衰落。

sentences.en: The empire was losing territory. European powers were dominating world politics.
sentences.zh: 帝国正在失去领土。欧洲列强主导着世界政治。

sentences.en: Many young officers, including Mustafa Kemal, started to realise that the Ottoman system was outdated, corrupt, and incapable of modernising.
sentences.zh: 许多年轻军官，包括穆斯塔法·凯末尔，开始意识到奥斯曼体系已经过时、腐败且无力实现现代化。

sentences.en: And it wasn’t just a realisation that these young men had, but a desire to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 这些年轻人不仅有了这种认识，而且还有改变现状的愿望。

sentences.en: Mustafa Kemal became part of a new generation of military leaders who wanted to reform, reshape, and modernise the country.
sentences.zh: 穆斯塔法·凯末尔成为了新一代军事领袖的一员，他们想要改革、重塑并使国家现代化。

sentences.en: After graduating, and with plenty of opportunities to hone his military chops, he quickly rose through the ranks.
sentences.zh: 毕业后，凭借大量磨炼军事技能的机会，他迅速晋升。

sentences.en: He fought in Libya against the Italians, in the Italo-Turkish war of 1911 and 1912.
sentences.zh: 他在1911年和1912年的意土战争中在利比亚与意大利人作战。

sentences.en: Then when war broke out in the Balkans, he went there.
sentences.zh: 后来巴尔干战争爆发，他又去了那里。

sentences.en: Everywhere he went, he distinguished himself.
sentences.zh: 无论走到哪里，他都表现出色。

sentences.en: He was young, but he was clearly a capable military leader.
sentences.zh: 他很年轻，但显然是一位有能力的军事领袖。

sentences.en: And then, in 1915, came the moment that would make him famous: Gallipoli.
sentences.zh: 接着，在1915年，让他成名的时刻到来了：加里波利（Gallipoli）。

sentences.en: A year into World War One, in a bid to defeat the Ottoman Empire, seize control of the Dardanelles Strait, and open up a vital supply route to Russia, British and French forces launched an ambitious naval and land invasion.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战爆发一年后，为了击败奥斯曼帝国、夺取达达尼尔海峡的控制权并打开通往俄罗斯的至关重要的补给线，英法军队发起了雄心勃勃的海上和陆地入侵。

sentences.en: Their target was Gallipoli, in the Eastern Mediterranean, which was guarded by the poorly equipped and under-prepared Ottoman Army.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是东地中海的加里波利，这里由装备落后、准备不足的奥斯曼军队防守。

sentences.en: Strategically, this mission made a lot of sense, and the British and French forces, two of the strongest military forces in the world, anticipated moving through the peninsula with minimal resistance.
sentences.zh: 从战略上讲，这项任务非常合乎逻辑，作为世界上最强大的两支军事力量，英法军队预计能够以最小的抵抗穿过半岛。

sentences.en: They grossly misjudged their opponents. After eight months of bloody fighting, with an estimated quarter of a million casualties on each side, the French and the British troops retreated.
sentences.zh: 他们严重误判了对手。经过八个月的血腥战斗，双方估计各有约二十五万人的伤亡后，英法军队撤退了。

sentences.en: Against all odds, the Ottomans won. And Mustafa Kemal, then only 34 years old, was one of the key commanders of this historic victory.
sentences.zh: 克服重重困难，奥斯曼人赢了。当时年仅34岁的穆斯塔法·凯末尔正是这场历史性胜利的关键指挥官之一。

sentences.en: It was during this battle that he gave one of his most famous orders to his men, an order that would go down in history as defining his character.
sentences.zh: 正是在这场战斗中，他向部下发出了他最著名的命令之一，这个命令将作为他性格的写照载入史册。

sentences.en: “I do not order you to attack,” he said, “I order you to die.”
sentences.zh: “我不是命令你们进攻，”他说，“我是命令你们去死。”

sentences.en: But while Gallipoli made him a hero, and provided plenty of soundbites to use later, it did not change the fate of the Ottoman Empire.
sentences.zh: 但加里波利虽然让他成为了英雄，并为日后提供了大量金句，却并没有改变奥斯曼帝国的命运。

sentences.en: The empire was still on the losing side of the war, and by 1918, it was collapsing.
sentences.zh: 帝国仍然处在战争失败的一方，到1918年，它正在崩溃。

sentences.en: The Sultan was powerless. Allied forces occupied Istanbul.
sentences.zh: 苏丹无权无势。盟军占领了伊斯坦布尔。

sentences.en: And the country that had once been feared and respected was on the chopping board, ready to be devoured by foreign enemies and powerless to do anything about it.
sentences.zh: 这个曾经令人敬畏和尊重的国家正处于砧板上，准备被外国敌人吞噬，而它却无能为力。

sentences.en: Now, it makes for a much better story to say that there was only one man who stood against all of this, and, were it not for Mustafa Kemal, Turkey would not exist.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果说只有一个站出来反对这一切的人，而且如果没有穆斯塔法·凯末尔，土耳其就不会存在，这样的故事听起来会精彩得多。

sentences.en: The reality seems to be that there were many other decorated generals and military leaders who were keen to stand up to the foreign powers, and had it not been Mustafa Kemal, it would most likely have been someone else.
sentences.zh: 但现实似乎是，还有许多其他声誉卓著的将军和军事领袖渴望挺身而出对抗外国列强，如果不是穆斯塔法·凯末尔，很可能也会是别人。

sentences.en: But history is full of what-ifs, and in the case of Turkey, it was not another general but Mustafa Kemal that would change the course of history.
sentences.zh: 然而历史充满了“如果”，就土耳其而言，改变历史进程的不是别的将军，正是穆斯塔法·凯末尔。

sentences.en: So, we are now at the starting point of Nutuk, the date at which Mustafa Kemal Atatürk begins the story of the Republic of Turkey.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们现在来到了 Nutuk 的起点，也就是穆斯塔法·凯末尔·阿塔图尔克开始讲述土耳其共和国故事的日期。

sentences.en: In May 1919, he boarded a ship and set sail for the northern coast of Anatolia, to the Black Sea port of Samsun.
sentences.zh: 1919年5月，他登上了一艘船，起航前往安纳托利亚北部海岸、黑海港口城市萨姆松。

sentences.en: When Mustafa Kemal arrived in Samsun on the 19th of May, 1919, he was still, officially at least, an officer in the Ottoman army.
sentences.zh: 1919年5月19日穆斯塔法·凯末尔抵达萨姆松时，从官方意义上讲，他仍然是奥斯曼军队的一名军官。

sentences.en: But in reality, he had already begun to set himself on a very different path.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他已经开始走上一条截然不同的道路。

sentences.en: He had been sent to Samsun by the Sultan’s government under the pretext of restoring order in Anatolia, but he had no intention of following orders from central command back in Istanbul.
sentences.zh: 他被苏丹政府派往萨姆松，借口是恢复安纳托利亚的秩序，但他根本不打算听从远在伊斯坦布尔的中央指挥部的命令。

sentences.en: Instead, he was about to launch what would become the Turkish War of Independence.
sentences.zh: 相反，他即将发起后来被称为土耳其独立战争的运动。

sentences.en: Now, this war went on for four years, and it warrants much more than just a passing mention in an episode.
sentences.zh: 这场战争持续了四年，在单集节目中绝不仅仅是一笔带过那么简单。

sentences.en: But, in short, the Greeks, the French, the British and the Armenians were all pushing into Anatolia from different directions.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，希腊人、法国人、英国人和亚美尼亚人当时都在从不同方向攻入安纳托利亚。

sentences.en: The Ottoman government and the Ottoman ruler, the Sultan, were doing little to intervene.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼政府和奥斯曼统治者苏丹几乎没有采取任何干预措施。

sentences.en: To many, it seemed as though the country was finished.
sentences.zh: 在许多人看来，这个国家似乎已经完了。

sentences.en: The Ottoman Empire had just lost a world war.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼帝国刚刚输掉了一场世界大战。

sentences.en: The Allies were in control. And there in the middle was a fledgling Turkish nationalist movement led by a quite popular but not universally known general.
sentences.zh: 盟军掌控了局势。而正中间则是一个初露头角的土耳其民族主义运动，由一位相当受欢迎但并非家喻户晓的将军领导。

sentences.en: How could a group of rebels, with limited weapons and no international support, stand a fighting chance?
sentences.zh: 一群武器有限且没有国际支持的叛军，怎么能有一线生机呢？

sentences.en: To cut a long story short, over the next three years, Mustafa Kemal turned a fragmented resistance into a disciplined army.
sentences.zh: 长话短说，在接下来的三年里，穆斯塔法·凯末尔将一支支离破碎的抵抗力量变成了一支纪律严明的军队。

sentences.en: He lured the Greeks inland, far away from their supply lines, and won a series of decisive battles.
sentences.zh: 他诱使希腊人深入内陆，远离他们的补给线，并赢得了多场决定性的胜利。

sentences.en: Now, you’ve heard that he went to military school and had spent practically his entire life in the army, but it’s hard to overstate quite how capable a military leader he was.
sentences.zh: 你已经听说过他上过军校，几乎把一生都奉献给了军队，但怎么强调他作为军事领袖的能力都不为过。

sentences.en: He was fearless on the battleground, had been injured multiple times, and had the scars to prove it.
sentences.zh: 他在战场上无所畏惧，曾多次受伤，身上的伤疤就是证明。

sentences.en: He was demanding to his soldiers, famously telling them that he expected them to die for their country at Gallipoli, and proclaiming that he would see the creation of a Turkish state, or he would die trying.
sentences.zh: 他对士兵要求严格，在加里波利曾说他期望士兵为国牺牲，并誓言要看到土耳其国的建立，否则死而后已，这番话流传千古。

sentences.en: All accounts point to a charismatic and brave leader; this was not a man who sat back at headquarters and moved around pretend soldiers on a map, this was a decorated, respected and highly effective military leader.
sentences.zh: 所有记录都指向一位富有领袖魅力且勇敢的领袖；他不是那种坐在指挥部里在地图上调兵遣将的人，而是一位战功卓著、备受尊敬且效率极高的军事领袖。

sentences.en: Now, fast forward to 1922, and against all the odds, the Turkish nationalists had pushed the foreign forces practically all the way out of Anatolia, and the Greek army was forced into a chaotic retreat towards the Aegean coast.
sentences.zh: 现在，时间快进到1922年，克服重重困难，土耳其民族主义者几乎将外国军队全部赶出了安纳托利亚，希腊军队被迫向爱琴海海岸混乱撤退。

sentences.en: The Turkish forces entered the coastal city of İzmir, and the war was effectively over.
sentences.zh: 土耳其军队进入了沿海城市伊兹密尔（İzmir），战争基本上结束了。

sentences.en: One by one, the occupying powers withdrew.
sentences.zh: 占领军一个接一个地撤走了。

sentences.en: The British, who were unwilling to risk another conflict, decided to negotiate.
sentences.zh: 不愿冒再次冲突风险的英国人决定通过谈判解决。

sentences.en: The result was The Treaty of Lausanne, which was signed in 1923.
sentences.zh: 其结果就是1923年签署的《洛桑条约》（The Treaty of Lausanne）。

sentences.en: It replaced the humiliating Treaty of Sèvres and declared that it would recognise the independence of a new Republic of Turkey.
sentences.zh: 它取代了那个屈辱的《色佛尔条约》，并宣布承认新土耳其共和国的独立。

sentences.en: Mustafa Kemal had done what seemed impossible.
sentences.zh: 穆斯塔法·凯末尔做到了看似不可能的事。

sentences.en: He had not only defeated the foreign occupiers, but he had also dismantled the Ottoman system itself.
sentences.zh: 他不仅击败了外国占领者，还瓦解了奥斯曼体系本身。

sentences.en: A few months later, on the 29th of October 1923, he declared the establishment of the Republic of Turkey, the Republic of Türkiye, to give it its correct modern name.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，即1923年10月29日，他宣布成立土耳其共和国（Republic of Türkiye，使用其正确的现代名称）。

sentences.en: Naturally, he would be its first president.
sentences.zh: 理所当然地，他成为了首任总统。

sentences.en: The Sultan, whose family had ruled the Ottoman Empire for 623 years, was deposed and sent into exile.
sentences.zh: 苏丹的家族统治了奥斯曼帝国623年，如今被废黜并流亡海外。

sentences.en: The Ottoman Empire, once one of the most powerful empires in the world, was no more.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼帝国这个曾经世界上最强大的帝国之一，不复存在了。

sentences.en: But Mustafa Kemal was not finished. The war was over, but now came the real challenge—building a modern nation from the ashes of an empire.
sentences.zh: 但穆斯塔法·凯末尔还没有结束。战争结束了，但真正的挑战现在才开始——从帝国的废墟中建立一个现代国家。

sentences.en: He had fought for Turkey’s independence, but now he would fight for its transformation.
sentences.zh: 他为土耳其的独立而战，但现在他要为土耳其的转型而战。

sentences.en: In his mind, independence was not enough.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，仅仅独立是不够的。

sentences.en: To truly survive in the modern world, Turkey had to change.
sentences.zh: 为了在现代世界中真正生存下去，土耳其必须改变。

sentences.en: And it had to change fast. He wasted no time.
sentences.zh: 而且必须迅速改变。他一刻也没有耽误。

sentences.en: Almost immediately, sweeping reforms began.
sentences.zh: 几乎立刻，激进的改革开始了。

sentences.en: And this wasn’t just about political structures.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅关乎政治结构。

sentences.en: It was about language, education, religion, culture, and the very way people saw themselves as citizens of a new republic.
sentences.zh: 它关乎语言、教育、宗教、文化，以及人们作为一个新共和国公民的自我认知方式。

sentences.en: One of the first and most radical changes was the abolition of the Caliphate in 1924.
sentences.zh: 最初也是最激进的变革之一是1924年废除哈里发制度。

sentences.en: For centuries, the Sultan of the Ottoman Empire had not just been a political ruler but also the spiritual leader of the Muslim world.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，奥斯曼帝国的苏丹不仅是政治统治者，也是穆斯林世界的精神领袖。

sentences.en: Many expected that even if the empire had collapsed, Turkey would retain this religious authority.
sentences.zh: 许多人曾预计，即使帝国崩溃，土耳其也会保留这种宗教权威。

sentences.en: But Mustafa Kemal had other ideas. He wanted Turkey to be a secular state, one where religious institutions had no influence over politics.
sentences.zh: 但穆斯塔法·凯末尔有不同的想法。他希望土耳其成为一个世俗国家，一个宗教机构对政治没有影响的国家。

sentences.en: This was shocking. The idea of separating Islam from government was unheard of in a Muslim-majority country.
sentences.zh: 这令人震惊。在一个穆斯林占多数的国家里，将伊斯兰教与政府分离的想法是前所未闻的。

sentences.en: And indeed, even today, most Muslim-majority countries have Islam as the official, state religion; they are not secular.
sentences.zh: 事实上，即使在今天，大多数穆斯林占多数的国家也将伊斯兰教定为官方国教；它们并非世俗国家。

sentences.en: As you might imagine, many opposed Atatürk’s decision.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的那样，许多人反对阿塔图尔克的决定。

sentences.en: But he pushed ahead. Religious schools were shut down.
sentences.zh: 但他勇往直前。宗教学校被关闭。

sentences.en: Islamic courts were abolished. Turkey was to be a modern, secular state.
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰法庭被废除。土耳其将成为一个现代的世俗国家。

sentences.en: This even came down to legislation around clothing.
sentences.zh: 这甚至延伸到了关于服装的立法。

sentences.en: And this brings us on to perhaps the best-known of the reforms: the decision to ban the fez.
sentences.zh: 这就让我们谈到了或许最著名的改革：禁止戴土耳其fez帽（土耳其红帽）的决定。

sentences.en: In case you didn’t know, a fez is that hat with no brim, no cap in the front.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道的话，fez帽是一种没有帽檐、前面没有帽舌的帽子。

sentences.en: It was particularly popular during the Ottoman Empire, and it was also practical for the majority Muslim population.
sentences.zh: 它在奥斯曼帝国时期特别受欢迎，对占多数的穆斯林人口来说也很实用。

sentences.en: Because it had no cap, no bit in the front, you could wear it during prayers, and touch your forehead to the ground.
sentences.zh: 因为它没有帽檐、前面没有凸起，你可以在礼拜时戴着它，让额头触地。

sentences.en: Kemal, so the story goes, was no great fan of this Islamic practice of prostrating yourself and touching your head on the floor, so he banned the hats that made this practice possible.
sentences.zh: 根据传说，凯末尔并不太喜欢这种五体投地、额头触地的伊斯兰习俗，于是他禁止了让这种习俗成为可能的帽子。

sentences.en: Instead, Turkish men were ordered to adopt European-style hats, which would help create a modern, Western-style identity for Turkey, and provide a clear break with the past.
sentences.zh: 相反，土耳其男子被命令改戴欧洲风格的帽子，这将有助于为土耳其创造一种现代的西方风格身份，并与过去彻底决裂。

sentences.en: Then came language reform. For centuries, the Turkish language had been written in Arabic script, and it also had a bunch of loan words from Persian and Arabic.
sentences.zh: 接着是语言改革。几个世纪以来，土耳其语一直用阿拉伯字母书写，其中还夹杂着大量波斯语和阿拉伯语的外来词。

sentences.en: As a result, it was a script that many found difficult to read and write.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多人觉得这种文字很难读写。

sentences.en: Mustafa Kemal wanted literacy rates to rise, and he believed that by simplifying the language, more people would be able to read and write.
sentences.zh: 穆斯塔法·凯末尔希望提高识字率，他相信通过简化语言，更多的人将能够识字。

sentences.en: A modern nation, after all, needed a modern, accessible language.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，一个现代国家需要一种现代的、易于掌握的语言。

sentences.en: And so, in 1928, he ordered the complete switch to the Latin alphabet.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1928年，他下令全面转向拉丁字母。

sentences.en: It was an extraordinary move. Overnight, books, newspapers, and street signs had to be rewritten.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非凡的举措。一夜之间，书籍、报纸和路标都必须重新编写。

sentences.en: Mustafa Kemal himself went from town to town, teaching people how to use the new script.
sentences.zh: 穆斯塔法·凯末尔亲自走访城镇，教人们如何使用新文字。

sentences.en: There are photos of him, the President, standing in front of a blackboard, chalk in hand, demonstrating the new style of writing.
sentences.zh: 有照片记录下他这位总统手拿粉笔站在黑板前，示范新书写方式的情景。

sentences.en: Education was another priority. The Ottoman Empire had an education system where religious and secular schools operated separately.
sentences.zh: 教育是另一个优先事项。奥斯曼帝国的教育系统是宗教学校和世俗学校分立的。

sentences.en: Mustafa Kemal scrapped this system entirely.
sentences.zh: 穆斯塔法·凯末尔彻底废除了这个系统。

sentences.en: A new, unified education system was put in place, free from religious influence.
sentences.zh: 建立了一个摆脱宗教影响的崭新、统一的教育系统。

sentences.en: Schools were to focus on science, mathematics, and modern subjects, subjects that would allow Turkey to compete in the modern world.
sentences.zh: 学校将专注于科学、数学和现代学科，这些学科将使土耳其能够在现代世界中竞争。

sentences.en: Women, too, saw dramatic changes under his leadership.
sentences.zh: 在领导下，女性的命运也发生了戏剧性的变化。

sentences.en: Under Ottoman rule, women had been largely excluded from public life.
sentences.zh: 在奥斯曼统治下，女性基本上被排除在公共生活之外。

sentences.en: But now, under the new republic, they were encouraged to work, study, and participate in politics.
sentences.zh: 但现在，在新共和国的体制下，她们被鼓励工作、学习并参与政治。

sentences.en: Women were granted the right to vote in Turkey in 1934, a fact that many Turkish people like to point out is earlier than in many European countries.
sentences.zh: 1934年，土耳其赋予了女性投票权，许多土耳其人喜欢指出，这一事实比许多欧洲国家还要早。

sentences.en: But these changes did not come without resistance.
sentences.zh: 但这些变革并非没有阻力。

sentences.en: Many in Turkey, particularly in the countryside, saw these reforms as an attack on their traditions.
sentences.zh: 土耳其的许多人，尤其是乡间的人，将这些改革视为对他们传统的攻击。

sentences.en: There were rebellions, opposition movements, and even assassination attempts.
sentences.zh: 叛乱、反对派运动甚至暗杀企图接踵而至。

sentences.en: But Mustafa Kemal was ruthless in his determination.
sentences.zh: 但穆斯塔法·凯末尔的决心冷酷无情。

sentences.en: He cracked down on dissent, exiling or imprisoning those who opposed his vision.
sentences.zh: 他严厉打击异见，将那些反对他愿景的人流放或关入监狱。

sentences.en: He believed there was no room for delay, no time for debate.
sentences.zh: 他认为没有容许拖延的余地，也没有时间辩论。

sentences.en: Turkey had to modernise, and it had to do it quickly.
sentences.zh: 土耳其必须实现现代化，而且必须迅速做到。

sentences.en: Now, there are those who criticised and still criticise his methods, but it is hard to argue about his effectiveness as the primary architect of the Turkey that exists today.
sentences.zh: 现在，确实有人过去和现在都在批评他的方法，但很难否认他作为当今土耳其主要缔造者的效率。

sentences.en: By the time he died in 1938, the country he left behind was unrecognisable from the Ottoman state he had been born into.
sentences.zh: 到1938年他去世时，他留下的国家与他出生时的奥斯曼帝国已经判若两国。

sentences.en: Turkey was a republic, not a sultanate. It had a secular government, a modern legal system, a new language, and an education system modelled on Western ideals.
sentences.zh: 土耳其是一个共和国，而不是苏丹国。它拥有世俗政府、现代法律体系、新语言以及以西方理想为蓝本的教育体系。

sentences.en: He was given the surname “Atatürk” in 1934, meaning “father of the Turks”.
sentences.zh: 他在1934年被授予“阿塔图尔克”的姓氏，意为“土耳其人之父”。

sentences.en: This was, in fact, the same year he introduced a law requiring all Turkish citizens to adopt a surname.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这正是他颁布法律要求所有土耳其公民采用姓氏的同一年。

sentences.en: Until then, as you heard about at the start of the episode, most people used only a first name and a title or patronymic, a name that signalled who their father was.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，正如你在本集开头听到的那样，大多数人只使用名和一个头衔或父名（表明他们父亲是谁的名字）。

sentences.en: But now, for the first time, every Turk was required to choose a family name.
sentences.zh: 但现在，所有土耳其人破天荒第一次被要求选择一个家族姓氏。

sentences.en: His given surname was, of course, ‘Atatürk’, meaning ‘Father of the Turks.
sentences.zh: 他被赋予的姓氏自然是“阿塔图尔克”，意为“土耳其人之父”。

sentences.en: Every year, at exactly 09:05 am on the 10th of November, the exact time ‘Atatürk’ died, the entire country of Turkey stops what it is doing to observe a minute’s silence.
sentences.zh: 每年11月10日上午09点05分，也就是“阿塔图尔克”逝世的准确时间，整个土耳其都会停下手头的工作，默哀一分钟。

sentences.en: Buses stop in the middle of the road, workers put down their tools, and TV chatshow hosts bow their heads in respect.
sentences.zh: 公交车停在路中央，工人们放下工具，电视脱口秀主持人低头以示敬意。

sentences.en: He might have been draconian at times, he has been called a dictator, but it is hard to argue that anybody is more deserving of the title “The father of modern Turkey”.
sentences.zh: 他有时可能会很严厉，甚至被人称为独裁者，但很难辩驳有谁比他更配得上“现代土耳其之父”这个称号。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天关于穆斯塔法·凯末尔·阿塔图尔克的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目很有趣，并且让你学到了新东西。

sentences.en: For the Turkish listeners out there, and the dozens of people who have asked me over the years to make an episode about Atatürk, I hope you in particular enjoyed it, and thought it did some justice to this clearly incredibly impressive leader.
sentences.zh: 对于收听节目的土耳其听众，以及多年来要求我制作一期关于阿塔图尔克节目的几十个人，我希望你们能特别喜欢它，并认为它算得上对这位显然极其伟大的领袖的一点致敬。

sentences.en: And as always, I would love to know what you thought about this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这期节目有什么看法。

sentences.en: What other interesting nuggets do you think people should know about Atatürk?
sentences.zh: 你认为人们还应该知道关于阿塔图尔克的哪些其他有趣的花絮？

sentences.en: Do you think Erdogan sees himself as a 21st-century Atatürk, and if so, how is this manifesting itself?
sentences.zh: 你认为埃尔多安（Erdogan）视自己为21世纪的阿塔图尔克吗？如果是这样，这又是如何表现出来的呢？

sentences.en: I would love to know. If you’re listening to this somewhere that allows you to comment, like Spotify or YouTube, just add a comment below.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道。如果你在 Spotify 或 YouTube 这样允许评论的平台上收听，请在下方留言。

sentences.en: And for the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 至于各位会员，你可以直接进入我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他充满好奇心的听众畅聊。

sentences.en: And as a quick reminder, next up on this loosely Ottoman-themed mini-series will be episodes on Ali Pasha, the so-called “Lion of Ioannina”, and the divided island of Cyprus.
sentences.zh: 简单提醒一下，这个大致以奥斯曼为主题的迷你系列的下一期节目将是关于阿里·帕夏（Ali Pasha，所谓的“约阿尼纳之狮”）以及分裂的塞浦路斯岛的节目。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是阿拉斯泰尔·巴奇，请注意安全，我们下期节目再见。
